lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details:
Listen and say introduces the new target vocabulary.
Listen and say gives students an opportunity to practise saying the target words.
Then practise introduces the lessons key structure ‘that’ to talk about things that are far away.
Look for careful listening, clear sounds, and confident repetition.
“I’ve got my invisible friend Martha here today. Where she’s from, schools look a little different. Can you help her learn what we have in our classroom?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - B Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice of the target vocabulary and using the structure What’s that…? It’s a….
Look for accurate and confident identification of the words and correct use of the structure (‘that’ not ‘this’ as in the previous lesson).
“Great work. She’s still got a lot of questions about what everything is called though. Can you practice helping her?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.67 - A Read and match

details: Read and match strengthens recognition of target words with word-picture matching reinforcing whole-word memory.
Look for clear, neat lines and correct word-picture matching.
“Let’s label these pictures to help her remember what everything is called. Then she’ll find it much easier to remember.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.67 - B Look and write

details: Look and write gives students controlled practice identifying and spelling the target words from the previous exercise. It reinforces letter order, and neat handwriting.
Look for correct word choice and spelling, consistent letter formation, and neat handwriting within the lines.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - Speaking Guessing game Put the cards face down. Pick a card and ask. Then guess and answer.

details: The guessing game provides the opportunity to further use the target vocabulary and structure in a more engaging way.
Look for correct placement of cards (‘this’ cards closer than ‘that’ cards) and mostly correct use of ‘What’s this/that…?’
“She’s just told me, she’s really confused about when we use ‘this’ and ‘that’. Can you play this game to help her understand?.”
